actions.detail: Switch to a cream or milk cleanser, drop foaming formulas and scrubs, and use lukewarm water only. Redness-prone skin recovers fastest when irritation sources are removed.
actions.title: Simplify to a barrier-friendly cleanser

actions.detail: Apply a niacinamide (4-5%) or centella serum to damp skin each morning, then a ceramide moisturizer. This combination visibly calms baseline redness within 2-4 weeks.
actions.title: Add niacinamide + ceramides

actions.detail: Use a zinc-based mineral sunscreen daily and track triggers (heat, spicy food, alcohol, stress) in a note for two weeks so you can remove the biggest one.
actions.title: Protect from UV and find your triggers

finding: Skin redness is above the healthy baseline — the skin barrier is likely irritated or reactive.

actions.detail: Use a salicylic acid (BHA) exfoliant 2-3 evenings per week on clean, dry skin. It clears congestion inside the pore, which is what rough texture actually is.
actions.title: Add a BHA exfoliant 2-3x/week

actions.detail: Wash pillowcases twice a week and clean your phone screen weekly — both press bacteria and oil into the skin every night.
actions.title: Fix the pillowcase and phone habit

actions.detail: Keep showers lukewarm and short; hot water strips the barrier and makes texture worse over time.
actions.title: Drop hot water on the face

finding: Skin texture is rough — congestion and dead-cell buildup are dulling the surface.

actions.detail: Get 7-9 hours of sleep and finish your last meal 2-3 hours before bed. Most under-eye darkness is a sleep problem wearing a skincare costume.
actions.title: Fix sleep first — it is the main lever

actions.detail: Apply a caffeine-based eye cream with gentle tapping each morning (never rub), and sleep on your back with your head slightly elevated to reduce morning puffiness.
actions.title: Morning eye routine with caffeine

actions.detail: Reduce salty late-night meals and cut late-night screen time — both worsen puffiness and eye strain overnight.
actions.title: Cut salty nights and late screens

finding: Under-eye darkness is pronounced — usually driven by short sleep, fluid retention, or thin skin showing through.

actions.detail: A textured fringe or volume on top balances a short forehead or long midface; a side-swept style softens a dominant lower third. Ask a barber for the specific fix, not just a shorter cut.
actions.title: Use a haircut to rebalance proportions

actions.detail: Keep facial hair deliberate: short sides with a fuller chin lengthens a compressed lower third; a cleaner cheek line sharpens a long midface.
actions.title: Shape facial hair with intention

actions.detail: Daily chin tucks and wall angels improve head posture — a forward head makes facial thirds look more unbalanced in photos than they are.
actions.title: Fix forward head posture

finding: Facial thirds are uneven — the forehead, midface, and lower face are not in the balanced 1:1:1 proportion.

actions.detail: Hold the phone at eye level and face the camera straight-on; a tilted head or angled camera creates most of the asymmetry you see in selfies.
actions.title: Fix camera angle before anything else

actions.detail: Sleep on your back and avoid always chewing on one side — both create subtle real asymmetry over years.
actions.title: Stop one-sided habits

actions.detail: Every face is asymmetric; styling (part direction, brow grooming) can visually balance a stronger side without any intervention.
actions.title: Balance with styling, not procedures

finding: Facial symmetry is below average — some of this is real, but much of it is usually photo angle and habits.

actions.detail: A structured resistance program 4-5x/week with a small calorie surplus builds the masseter-adjacent structure and overall frame that make a jawline read stronger.
actions.title: Build the frame with resistance training

actions.detail: Cut added sugar, limit alcohol, and walk after meals — facial leanness responds quickly to lower water retention and body fat.
actions.title: Lean out the face through diet

actions.detail: Keep the beard short on the sides and slightly fuller at the chin, with a clean cheek line — this visually sharpens the jaw angle.
actions.title: Beard shaping for jaw definition

finding: Jaw-to-cheekbone ratio is on the narrow side — the lower face reads softer than the midface.

actions.detail: Eat at a 15-20% calorie deficit with 2.0-2.2g of protein per kg of bodyweight — the face leans out noticeably in the first 4-6 weeks.
actions.title: Start a structured cut

actions.detail: Lift 4x/week (upper/lower split) during the cut — muscle retention is what keeps the face and body looking defined rather than just smaller.
actions.title: Train to keep muscle while cutting

actions.detail: Walk 10,000 steps daily and take a short walk after meals — low-effort movement that quietly deepens the deficit.
actions.title: Add daily walking

finding: Estimated body fat is above the lean range — a cut will sharpen the jawline and cheekbones more than any other single change.

actions.detail: Set a fixed wake time (even on weekends), get daylight within an hour of waking, and keep the bedroom dark and cool. Consistency beats duration.
actions.title: Anchor a fixed sleep schedule

actions.detail: Finish eating 2-3 hours before bed, cut caffeine after noon, and dim screens in the last hour. Most poor sleep is a late-evening problem.
actions.title: Fix the last two hours of the day

actions.detail: Short sleep raises hunger hormones and cortisol, which shows up as breakouts, dullness, and under-eye darkness. Treat sleep as a skincare step.
actions.title: Treat sleep as skincare

finding: Sleep is under 7 hours — the single biggest drag on skin recovery, eye appearance, and fat loss.

actions.detail: Build each meal around a palm-sized protein portion, vegetables, and a whole carb. Under-eating protein shows on the face first.
actions.title: Anchor meals on protein

actions.detail: Cut sugary drinks and halve added sugar in snacks — sugar spikes are a direct breakout and dullness trigger.
actions.title: Cut liquid sugar and added sugar

actions.detail: Add a daily fermented food (curd/yogurt) and fiber-rich vegetables — gut health is closely tied to skin clarity.
actions.title: Feed the gut-skin link

finding: Diet quality is poor — skin, energy, and body composition all suffer before anything else does.
